questions.stem: A project is best defined as a temporary endeavor undertaken to create a

options.A: unique product or service

questions.explanation: A project is a temporary and unique endeavor with a defined start and end, aimed at producing a unique product, service, or result.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a project?

options.A: Temporary nature

questions.explanation: Projects are unique and temporary. Repetitive processes are characteristics of operations, not projects.

questions.stem: Project management is the application of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to project activities to

options.A: meet project requirements

questions.explanation: The core purpose of project management is to apply competencies and resources to successfully meet the defined project requirements.

questions.stem: The triple constraint in project management refers to

options.A: Scope, time, and cost

questions.explanation: The triple constraint (iron triangle) consists of scope, time, and cost - any change to one affects the others.

questions.stem: A project charter is a document that formally

options.A: authorises the existence of a project

questions.explanation: The project charter officially authorises the project and gives the project manager the authority to apply organisational resources.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a programme in project management?

options.A: A group of related projects managed in a coordinated way

questions.explanation: A programme is a collection of related projects managed together to obtain benefits not available from managing them individually.

questions.stem: The primary role of a project manager is to

options.A: lead the team to achieve project goals

questions.explanation: A project manager is responsible for planning, executing, and closing projects while leading the team toward the project objectives.

questions.stem: Project scope refers to

options.A: the work required to deliver a project's objectives
options.D: the time allocated to the project

questions.explanation: Project scope defines all the work and only the work that must be done to complete the project deliverables successfully.

questions.stem: A milestone in a project is best described as

options.A: a significant event or achievement

questions.explanation: A milestone marks a key point or significant achievement in the project timeline, often used to track progress.

questions.stem: Portfolio management in project management involves

options.A: managing a collection of projects aligned to strategic goals
options.B: managing one project at a time

questions.explanation: Portfolio management centralises the oversight of projects and programmes to align them with organisational strategy and optimise resources.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a project deliverable?

options.A: A tangible or intangible outcome produced by the project

questions.explanation: Deliverables are specific outputs that must be produced to complete a project or a phase of a project.

questions.stem: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) is used to

options.A: decompose project work into manageable components

questions.explanation: The WBS breaks down the total scope of work into smaller, more manageable pieces to improve planning and control.

questions.stem: The concept of 'scope creep' in project management refers to

options.A: uncontrolled changes or growth in project scope

questions.explanation: Scope creep is the gradual, uncontrolled expansion of project scope without adjustments to time, cost, or resources.

questions.stem: A baseline in project management is best defined as

options.A: an approved plan used as a reference for measuring performance

questions.explanation: A baseline is the original approved version of a project plan (scope, schedule, or cost) against which performance is measured.

questions.stem: Which knowledge area focuses on ensuring stakeholder needs are identified and met throughout the project?

options.A: Stakeholder management

questions.explanation: Stakeholder management involves identifying, analysing, and managing the expectations and needs of all project stakeholders.

questions.stem: A project bottleneck is best described as

options.A: a constraint that limits the overall throughput of a project

questions.explanation: A bottleneck is any resource, process, or dependency that restricts the flow of work and slows overall project progress.

questions.stem: The Theory of Constraints (TOC) in project management focuses on

options.A: identifying and eliminating the weakest link in a process

questions.explanation: TOC, developed by Eliyahu Goldratt, focuses on identifying the system's primary constraint and improving it to increase throughput.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common cause of project bottlenecks?

options.A: Resource over-allocation

questions.explanation: When resources are over-committed or under-available, work queues build up causing delays and bottlenecks in project execution.

questions.stem: Resource levelling as a solution to bottlenecks involves

options.A: adjusting the schedule to balance resource demand and supply

questions.explanation: Resource levelling resolves over-allocation by shifting task dates to ensure resources are not over-committed at any point in time.

questions.stem: Fast-tracking as a bottleneck solution refers to

options.A: performing sequential activities in parallel

questions.explanation: Fast-tracking compresses the project schedule by running activities simultaneously that were originally planned sequentially.

questions.stem: Crashing a project schedule to resolve bottlenecks involves

options.A: adding resources to critical path activities to shorten duration

questions.explanation: Crashing involves adding extra resources (people, equipment, funds) to critical path tasks to reduce their duration and resolve schedule bottlenecks.

questions.stem: Which tool is most effective for visually identifying where bottlenecks occur in a workflow?

options.A: Kanban board

questions.explanation: Kanban boards visualise work-in-progress and make bottlenecks visible by showing where tasks accumulate in the workflow.

questions.stem: A project buffer in Critical Chain Project Management (CCPM) is used to

options.A: protect the project completion date from uncertainties

questions.explanation: CCPM uses project buffers placed at the end of the critical chain to absorb delays and protect the final delivery date.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a resource bottleneck?

options.A: When a key resource is required by multiple tasks simultaneously
options.B: When a project has no defined objectives
options.D: When a project has excess budget

questions.explanation: A resource bottleneck occurs when a single resource (person, equipment, etc.) is demanded by multiple concurrent tasks, creating a capacity constraint.

questions.stem: Outsourcing certain project activities is considered a bottleneck solution because it

options.A: transfers work to external parties, freeing internal capacity
options.B: eliminates the need for project planning

questions.explanation: Outsourcing relieves internal resource constraints by delegating specific tasks to vendors or contractors who have the required capacity.

questions.stem: The critical path in a project network is significant because it

options.A: determines the shortest possible project duration

questions.explanation: The critical path is the longest sequence of dependent activities and determines the minimum time required to complete the project.

questions.stem: Process automation as a bottleneck solution is best described as

options.A: using technology to perform repetitive tasks faster and more reliably
options.B: manual review of all project tasks

questions.explanation: Automation removes human bottlenecks in repetitive processes, improving speed, consistency, and freeing team members for higher-value work.

questions.stem: Which analysis technique helps a project team identify root causes of bottlenecks?

options.A: Fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram

questions.explanation: The fishbone diagram is a cause-and-effect tool that helps teams systematically identify the root causes of a problem or bottleneck.

questions.stem: A Gantt chart is primarily used in project management to

options.A: display the project schedule against a timeline

questions.explanation: A Gantt chart is a bar chart that visually represents the project schedule, showing start/end dates for tasks against a calendar timeline.

questions.stem: PERT stands for

options.A: Programme Evaluation and Review Technique

questions.explanation: PERT is a statistical tool used in project management for analysing and representing tasks involved in completing a project.

questions.stem: The Critical Path Method (CPM) is used to

options.A: identify the longest path of dependent tasks in a project

questions.explanation: CPM identifies the sequence of crucial steps that determines the minimum project duration and helps focus management attention.

questions.stem: Earned Value Management (EVM) is a technique used to measure

options.A: project performance and progress against the baseline

questions.explanation: EVM integrates scope, schedule, and cost measurements to provide an objective assessment of project performance and forecasts.

questions.stem: In Earned Value Management, the Schedule Performance Index (SPI) is calculated as

options.A: Earned Value divided by Planned Value
options.B: Actual Cost divided by Earned Value
options.C: Budget at Completion minus Actual Cost
options.D: Planned Value divided by Actual Cost

questions.explanation: SPI = EV / PV. An SPI greater than 1 indicates the project is ahead of schedule; less than 1 means it is behind schedule.

questions.stem: A RACI matrix is used in project management to

options.A: clarify roles and responsibilities for project tasks

questions.explanation: RACI (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed) is a matrix that defines who does what in a project, preventing confusion over roles.

questions.stem: Risk registers in project management are used to

options.A: document identified risks, their impacts, and response plans

questions.explanation: A risk register is a living document that captures all identified risks, their probability, impact, and the planned risk responses.

questions.stem: Which technique uses three time estimates (optimistic, pessimistic, most likely) to calculate task duration?

options.A: PERT

questions.explanation: PERT uses three estimates - optimistic (O), pessimistic (P), and most likely (M) - to calculate expected duration: (O + 4M + P) / 6.

questions.stem: A project dashboard is best described as

options.A: a visual summary of key project metrics and status indicators

questions.explanation: Project dashboards provide at-a-glance visibility into project health using KPIs, traffic lights, and charts for quick decision-making.

questions.stem: Which project management tool is used to visually represent the hierarchical breakdown of project deliverables?

options.A: Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

questions.explanation: The WBS is a hierarchical decomposition of the total project scope into manageable components called work packages.

questions.stem: The purpose of a project communication plan is to

options.A: define how project information will be shared among stakeholders

questions.explanation: A communication plan outlines who receives what information, when, in what format, and through which channels throughout the project.

questions.stem: Monte Carlo simulation in project management is used to

options.A: model the probability of different project outcomes

questions.explanation: Monte Carlo simulation runs thousands of scenarios using variable inputs to produce a probability distribution of possible project outcomes.

questions.stem: A project network diagram (precedence diagram) is used to

options.A: show the sequence and dependencies of project activities

questions.explanation: Network diagrams illustrate the logical relationships between project activities, enabling identification of the critical path and task dependencies.

questions.stem: Benchmarking as a project management technique involves

options.A: comparing project performance against industry standards or best practices

questions.explanation: Benchmarking evaluates project performance metrics against recognised standards to identify gaps and improvement opportunities.

questions.stem: A lessons-learned register is primarily used to

options.A: document knowledge gained for use in future projects

questions.explanation: A lessons-learned register captures insights about what worked and what did not during the project, improving future project delivery.

questions.stem: The Waterfall model in project management is characterised by

options.A: sequential phases where each must be completed before the next begins

questions.explanation: Waterfall is a linear, sequential methodology where progress flows downward through defined phases: requirements, design, implementation, verification, and maintenance.

questions.stem: Agile project management is best described as

options.A: an iterative approach that delivers value incrementally through collaboration
options.D: a method focused solely on documentation

questions.explanation: Agile embraces iterative development, customer collaboration, and responding to change over following a fixed plan.

questions.stem: The PRINCE2 methodology stands for

options.A: Projects IN Controlled Environments
options.B: Project Review and Integration in Complex Environments
options.C: Planned Resource Integration and Controlled Execution
options.D: Process Review Including New Control Evaluation

questions.explanation: PRINCE2 (Projects IN Controlled Environments) is a structured, process-based project management method widely used in the UK and internationally.

questions.stem: In Scrum, a Sprint is defined as

options.A: a time-boxed iteration typically lasting 1-4 weeks

questions.explanation: A Sprint is a fixed-length iteration in Scrum during which a potentially shippable product increment is created.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a key principle of the Agile Manifesto?

options.A: Responding to change over following a plan
options.D: Processes and tools over individuals and interactions

questions.explanation: The Agile Manifesto values responding to change over following a plan, reflecting the need for flexibility in dynamic project environments.

questions.stem: The PMBOK Guide is published by

options.A: Project Management Institute (PMI)

questions.explanation: The Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK) Guide is published by PMI and is a widely recognised standard for project management practices.

questions.stem: A key difference between traditional (Waterfall) and Agile project management is that

options.A: Agile embraces change while Waterfall resists it
options.B: Waterfall is iterative while Agile is sequential
options.C: Agile requires more documentation than Waterfall

questions.explanation: Traditional Waterfall methods resist changes after requirements are set, while Agile is designed to accommodate and welcome changing requirements.

questions.stem: Lean project management focuses primarily on

options.A: eliminating waste and maximising value delivery

questions.explanation: Lean, derived from manufacturing principles, aims to eliminate non-value-adding activities (waste) and improve flow to deliver maximum value.

questions.stem: In Scrum, the Product Owner is responsible for

options.A: managing and prioritising the product backlog

questions.explanation: The Product Owner is responsible for maximising the value of the product by managing and prioritising the product backlog.

questions.stem: The Six Sigma methodology primarily aims to

options.A: reduce defects and process variability to improve quality

questions.explanation: Six Sigma is a data-driven methodology that seeks to reduce defects to fewer than 3.4 per million opportunities through process improvement.

questions.stem: Hybrid project management combines elements of

options.A: both traditional and Agile methodologies

questions.explanation: Hybrid approaches blend predictive (traditional) and adaptive (Agile) elements to suit the specific needs of a project or organisation.

questions.stem: In PRINCE2, the principle of 'manage by exception' means

options.A: management only intervenes when tolerances are exceeded
options.C: team members manage their own projects

questions.explanation: Manage by exception delegates authority within defined tolerances; only when those tolerances are forecast to be breached does escalation occur.

questions.stem: The Kanban method in project management is based on

options.A: visualising workflow and limiting work in progress

questions.explanation: Kanban uses visual boards to represent workflow stages and enforces WIP limits to prevent bottlenecks and improve flow.

questions.stem: Which contemporary methodology uses the concept of 'sprints' and 'backlogs'?

options.A: Scrum

questions.explanation: Scrum is an Agile framework that organises work into sprints and uses a product backlog to manage and prioritise requirements.

questions.stem: The traditional project management approach is most suitable for projects that are

options.A: well-defined with stable requirements

questions.explanation: Traditional (Waterfall) methods work best when project requirements are clear, stable, and unlikely to change significantly during execution.

questions.stem: Stakeholders in a project are defined as

options.A: individuals or groups who may affect or be affected by the project
options.B: only the project sponsor and manager

questions.explanation: Stakeholders include anyone who has an interest in or is impacted by the project, including internal and external parties.

questions.stem: The project sponsor's primary role is to

options.A: provide resources and champion the project at executive level

questions.explanation: The project sponsor is the executive stakeholder responsible for funding, supporting, and championing the project within the organisation.

questions.stem: A Project Management Office (PMO) is responsible for

options.A: setting project management standards and supporting project delivery

questions.explanation: A PMO establishes governance frameworks, standardises PM practices, and provides support and oversight for projects across the organisation.

questions.stem: Which actor in project management has overall accountability for project success?

options.A: Project manager

questions.explanation: The project manager is accountable for planning, executing, and delivering the project within the agreed scope, time, cost, and quality.

questions.stem: End users in a project are best described as

options.A: those who will use the final product or service

questions.explanation: End users are the people who will ultimately use or benefit from the project's deliverables, making their requirements critical to project success.

questions.stem: A steering committee in project management is typically responsible for

options.A: providing strategic direction and resolving escalated issues

questions.explanation: A steering committee provides governance and strategic oversight, approves major decisions, and resolves issues escalated beyond the project manager's authority.

questions.stem: In Scrum, the Scrum Master's role is to

options.A: facilitate the process and remove impediments for the team

questions.explanation: The Scrum Master is a servant-leader who coaches the team, facilitates Scrum events, and removes obstacles to the team's progress.

questions.stem: A project team member's primary responsibility is to

options.A: execute assigned work packages and deliver agreed outputs

questions.explanation: Team members are responsible for completing the technical or specialist tasks assigned to them within the project plan.

questions.stem: An external consultant in a project typically provides

options.A: specialist expertise that is not available internally

questions.explanation: External consultants are engaged to bring specific knowledge, skills, or capacity that the organisation lacks internally for the project.

questions.stem: Which stakeholder analysis tool maps stakeholders based on their power and interest?

options.A: Power/Interest grid

questions.explanation: The Power/Interest grid categorises stakeholders into four quadrants to guide how much engagement and management attention each group requires.

questions.stem: A functional manager in a project context is responsible for

options.A: providing and managing resources from their department

questions.explanation: In matrix organisations, functional managers own the resources (staff) and must balance departmental work with project demands.

questions.stem: The concept of a 'champion' in project management refers to

options.A: an advocate who promotes and supports the project within the organisation
options.B: the most technically skilled team member
options.C: the person who writes the project plan

questions.explanation: A project champion actively advocates for the project, helps secure resources and support, and overcomes organisational resistance.

questions.stem: Negative stakeholders in project management are those who

options.A: see the project as having a negative impact on their interests
options.B: are always external to the organisation
options.C: have no interest in the project
options.D: are contractors hired to review the project

questions.explanation: Negative stakeholders oppose the project because they believe it will harm their interests; their concerns must be managed proactively.

questions.stem: The project lifecycle is defined as

options.A: the series of phases that a project passes through from initiation to closure
options.B: the annual review process of a project

questions.explanation: The project lifecycle describes the logical sequence of phases a project goes through, from its beginning to its end.

questions.stem: Which phase of the project lifecycle involves defining project objectives and feasibility?

options.A: Initiation

questions.explanation: The initiation phase establishes the project purpose, assesses feasibility, defines high-level objectives, and produces the project charter.

questions.stem: During the planning phase of a project, the main activity is

options.A: developing detailed plans for scope, schedule, cost, and risk

questions.explanation: The planning phase produces the project management plan, which guides execution and control by detailing how the project will be delivered.

questions.stem: The execution phase of a project is primarily concerned with

options.A: carrying out the work defined in the project plan

questions.explanation: During execution, project team members perform the work packages, produce deliverables, and manage stakeholder engagement.

questions.stem: The monitoring and controlling phase of a project involves

options.A: tracking performance and implementing corrective actions

questions.explanation: Monitoring and controlling involves measuring project performance against the baseline and taking corrective action when deviations occur.

questions.stem: The closure phase of a project includes which of the following activities?

options.A: Formal acceptance of deliverables and lessons-learned documentation

questions.explanation: Project closure involves obtaining formal sign-off on deliverables, releasing resources, archiving records, and documenting lessons learned.

questions.stem: A feasibility study conducted during project initiation is used to

options.A: assess whether the project is viable and worth pursuing

questions.explanation: A feasibility study evaluates technical, financial, operational, and legal dimensions to determine if the project is achievable and worthwhile.

questions.stem: Phase gates (stage gates) in a project lifecycle are used to

options.A: review progress and approve continuation to the next phase

questions.explanation: Phase gates are formal review points at which a decision is made to proceed, modify, or stop the project before moving to the next phase.

questions.stem: Cost and staffing levels in a project are typically

options.A: low at the start, highest during execution, and decrease at closure

questions.explanation: Resource usage and costs follow a bell curve: low at initiation, peak during execution, and taper off during closure.

questions.stem: The risk of project failure is generally

options.A: highest at the beginning of the project and decreases over time

questions.explanation: Risk is greatest at the start of a project when uncertainty is highest; as more decisions are made and work is done, risk generally decreases.

questions.stem: During which lifecycle phase is the project management plan formally approved?

options.A: Planning

questions.explanation: The project management plan is developed and approved during the planning phase before project execution begins.

questions.stem: A post-project review (post-mortem) is conducted during which phase?

options.A: Closure

questions.explanation: A post-project review is performed during closure to evaluate what went well, what went wrong, and what can be improved in future projects.

questions.stem: Iterative lifecycles differ from predictive lifecycles in that they

options.A: allow for repeated cycles of work to refine the deliverable
options.B: complete all planning before any work begins
options.D: require fixed scope from the start

questions.explanation: Iterative lifecycles revisit earlier phases repeatedly to refine outputs based on feedback, unlike predictive lifecycles that follow a linear sequence.

questions.stem: Project delivery process refers to

options.A: the systematic activities used to complete and hand over project outputs

questions.explanation: The project delivery process encompasses all activities from planning through execution to handover, ensuring outputs meet requirements.

questions.stem: A change control process in project management is designed to

options.A: manage and approve changes to project scope, schedule, or cost

questions.explanation: Change control ensures that proposed changes are formally evaluated, approved, and documented to prevent uncontrolled scope creep.

questions.stem: Quality assurance in project delivery involves

options.A: auditing processes to ensure standards are being followed

questions.explanation: Quality assurance focuses on the processes used to produce deliverables, ensuring they comply with defined quality standards.

questions.stem: Quality control in project delivery is focused on

options.A: inspecting deliverables to verify they meet specified requirements

questions.explanation: Quality control involves monitoring and inspecting specific project outputs to ensure they conform to defined quality standards.

questions.stem: Procurement management in project delivery involves

options.A: acquiring goods and services from external suppliers

questions.explanation: Procurement management covers the processes of planning, acquiring, and managing contracts for external resources needed by the project.

questions.stem: A project kickoff meeting is typically held

options.A: at the beginning of execution to align the team on objectives and plans

questions.explanation: The kickoff meeting formally marks the start of project execution, ensuring all stakeholders share a common understanding of the project plan.

questions.stem: Handover and transition in project delivery refers to

options.A: transferring the completed deliverable to the client or operations team

questions.explanation: Handover ensures the project's outputs are formally transferred to those who will use or operate them, including training and documentation.

questions.stem: Integrated change control in project delivery ensures that

options.A: all changes are considered in relation to their impact on the entire project
options.D: the project manager approves all changes unilaterally

questions.explanation: Integrated change control evaluates how a change affects all aspects of the project (scope, schedule, cost, quality, risk) before approval.

questions.stem: A project status report serves to

options.A: communicate project progress, issues, and forecasts to stakeholders

questions.explanation: Status reports provide regular updates on schedule, budget, scope, risks, and issues to keep stakeholders informed and decisions timely.

questions.stem: Issue management in project delivery involves

options.A: identifying, logging, and resolving problems that have already occurred

questions.explanation: Issue management deals with current problems (unlike risk management which handles future uncertainties) and tracks them to resolution.

questions.stem: Configuration management in project delivery is used to

options.A: control changes to project documentation and deliverables

questions.explanation: Configuration management ensures that all versions of project documents and deliverables are tracked, controlled, and consistent.

questions.stem: Acceptance criteria in project delivery define

options.A: the conditions a deliverable must meet to be accepted by the client
options.D: the risk tolerance of the organisation

questions.explanation: Acceptance criteria are measurable conditions agreed upon before delivery, used to verify that outputs meet the client's requirements.

questions.stem: User Acceptance Testing (UAT) in project delivery is performed by

options.A: end users to verify the deliverable meets their business requirements

questions.explanation: UAT allows end users to test the deliverable in real-world conditions to confirm it meets their needs before formal acceptance.

questions.stem: Scope verification in project delivery involves

options.A: formally reviewing and accepting completed deliverables with the client

questions.explanation: Scope verification (now called 'Validate Scope' in PMBOK) is the process of obtaining formal client acceptance of completed project deliverables.

questions.stem: Continuous improvement within a project delivery environment is best supported by

options.A: regular retrospectives and lessons-learned reviews

questions.explanation: Retrospectives and lessons-learned sessions enable teams to reflect, identify improvements, and apply them within or across projects.

questions.stem: The primary purpose of a project closure report is to

options.A: formally document project performance, outcomes, and recommendations for future projects

questions.explanation: The closure report summarises actual vs planned performance, captures lessons learned, and provides a formal record of the project's outcome.
